previous_history.note: Historical Phase 1 research is preserved and not deleted. This update adds Phase 2 evidence only.

strategy_changes.change: Progressively escalate through source, state/data-flow, sequence search, gas/resource analysis, Yul/IR, and bytecode/opcode analysis when the public source is insufficient.
strategy_changes.why: Phase 2 challenges intentionally hide crucial behavior behind state-history coupling and assembly-level data interpretation.

strategy_changes.change: Treat abi/calldata and storage aliasing as first-class hypotheses rather than just source-level gas loops.
strategy_changes.why: The Phase 2 challenge set includes an EVM-level assembly path where source-only reasoning fails.

strategy_changes.change: Require a minimized counterexample and replay-backed evidence before promoting a finding to confirmed.
strategy_changes.why: Separation between the blind benchmark and hidden ground truth makes public-only speculation risky and easy to overfit.

strategy_changes.change: Keep failed experiments and missed mechanisms as explicit records instead of deleting them or recasting them as discoveries.
strategy_changes.why: The benchmark design explicitly requires recording misses and false positives to preserve the honesty of the research history.

phase_1_vs_phase_2_improvement.phase_1: Public benchmarks exposed mostly state-growth and loop-bound effects with straightforward source-level causes.
phase_1_vs_phase_2_improvement.phase_2: Blind benchmarks require call-order reasoning, cross-function state carries, and assembly-level interpretation for the harder cases.
phase_1_vs_phase_2_improvement.adjustment: The research planner now prioritizes sequence fuzzing and deeper EVM-layer analysis for later-stage challenge families.
